_note: Batch 2 (post round-1 review). 4 sci-fi theme tag sets completing the sample set of 10 (#0 original + 5 batch1 + 4 here). SEEDS for the world-gen pipeline (storybrain/generator). Requirements: sci-fi, artifacts, alien civilizations (need NOT be fallen). Resource tie-ins welcome but not mandatory. Psychic OPTIONAL (per Sam) — kept light (3 none / 1 subtle), NOT piled on. Breadth is the goal: each must produce worlds distinct from the others, from batch1, and from theme #0 (the marrow/Velt/Choir world in generator/world-scifi.json: fallen-civ + resource-exploitation-of-a-living-organism-gone-terribly-wrong + overt psychic cascade + reconstruct-the-linear-fall). The decisive test per batch1's reviews is the MYSTERY SPINE: each seed must imply a structurally different story shape than #0's linear cause->escalation->collapse autopsy. Spines here: AWE/where-did-they-go (megastructure), OUTBREAK/containment-race (plague), MERCANTILE/whose-history-is-real (trade), STEWARDSHIP/are-we-the-experiment (uplift). ALIEN_STATUS CONTROLLED VOCABULARY (use exactly these): living (present, conscious, agency now) | active (present, operating, non-communicative/indifferent) | ambiguous (alive-or-dead genuinely undecided) | absent (makers gone — left or vanished, NOT a witnessed fall) | hidden (present and acting but never seen) | dormant (sleeping, wakeable) | extinct (gone, only a corpse-civ remains) | ancestral (the makers are our forebears) | fallen (witnessed collapse — reserved for #0-style autopsies, avoided here). RESOURCE_CENTRALITY: none | low | moderate | high | core. PIPELINE CAVEAT (carried from batch1 round-3): generator/prompt-canon.md + schema.ts currently hard-code status:'fallen|extant', a MANDATORY civ-tied psychic power, and a mystery shaped as a caused_by fall-chain (validateWorld() HARD-FAILS anything else; check.ts exits nonzero, load.ts refuses to load). These seeds DELIBERATELY use statuses (absent/extinct/living/hidden), non-fall mystery spines (awe/race/mercantile/stewardship), and mostly-none psychic that the current pipeline would reject or coerce back toward #0. Treat them as the SPEC for generalizing the enum + the mystery shape + making psychic genuinely optional, NOT as conforming to today's contract.

sets.title: The Inheritance
sets.hook: Humanity arrives INSIDE a working megastructure the size of a solar system — and its builders are simply GONE. No bodies, no war, no graves, no autopsy to perform: this is not a fall, and they were not us. The artifacts are control-keys that switch dormant pieces of the structure back on; each activation lights a new region and a new clue. The mystery is not how they died but where they WENT, and what this thing was built to DO — and whether finishing what they started is a gift or a trap.
sets.artifact_flavor: Control-keys and access-sigils that wake dormant megastructure systems. Power and matter ARE here in vast quantity, but exploiting them is instrumental, not the point: every key you find both lights up usable capacity AND drops a fragment of the builders' purpose — and risks waking a subsystem that was switched off for a reason. The hunt is light-the-machine-piece-by-piece, where each light is also a clue.
sets.distinct_from_siblings: Scale and AWE, not bodies and not a fall. Aliens left no corpse to excavate (vs #0 and plague) and no live presence to negotiate with (vs trade) — only an inhabited machine and an unanswered 'why'. Distinct from gen-ship's `absent` too: those makers erased themselves and turn out to be us; these are genuinely OTHER, genuinely vanished, and the spine is what-was-it-for, not it-was-us. Resource is high but serves the awe-mystery, never replaces it.

sets.title: The Quarantine Worlds
sets.hook: An alien civilization was consumed by a self-replicating extinction-vector (gray-goo / memetic / biological) it failed to contain. But this is NOT a fall to reconstruct — their death is settled backstory. The story is in the PRESENT TENSE: the vector is still out there, dormant in sealed worlds and live in drifting carriers, and your colony is now inside its range. Hunting the quarantined relics and scattered cure-fragments is a RACE to assemble containment before it reaches you — and every relic you crack might be the cure or the next outbreak.
sets.artifact_flavor: Sealed quarantine-relics and cure-fragments, each a LIVE hazard. Assembling the right set yields containment or a vaccine; opening the wrong one reseeds the plague here, now. The hunt has a real downside the player can lose by — you can spread the very thing you sought. The generative variable is the vector's NATURE per world (nanite swarm / mind-virus that spreads through the relics' lore / engineered pathogen), which changes what containment even means.
sets.distinct_from_siblings: Spine is OUTBREAK / containment-race, present tense — explicitly NOT #0's autopsy of how-they-fell. The aliens are victims of an EXTERNAL killer, not authors of their own greed-driven collapse. The hunt is a clock with a fail-state (reseed the plague), unlike megastructure's awe-stroll or trade's deal-making. Resource is low: the engine is containment, not extraction, so this set deliberately does NOT lean on the resource pillar.

sets.title: The Long Bazaar
sets.hook: The galaxy is ALIVE and crowded — dozens of minor alien species trading, scheming, and feuding across a busy frontier. No grand empire, no tomb, no single mind: a marketplace. Artifacts are black-market curios whose power is inseparable from their PROVENANCE — and half the provenance is forged. The resource is a contested commodity everyone wants a cut of. The story is whose history is even real, who you deal with, and who you cross to get it.
sets.artifact_flavor: Curios and relics moving on a black market, where an artifact's power depends on a (often forged) provenance chain. The HUNT is find-and-authenticate: track a rumored relic across living factions, then prove (or fake, or break) its history — a social/spatial chase that ends in a deal, a heist, or a forgery, not a dig. The generative engine is the FACTION WEB + the specific contested commodity: worlds diverge on WHO is feuding over WHAT, so no two read as the same bazaar.
sets.distinct_from_siblings: The only LIVED-IN, crowded, mercantile galaxy of many SHALLOW transactional factions — distinct from first-contact's single attentive alien gatekeeper (there the puzzle is YOUR worthiness; here it's the RELIC'S history). Tone is noir/political; the 'civilization' is a market, and the mystery is whose-provenance-is-real, not why-anyone-fell. Distinct from #0 in every axis: living aliens, social spine, no collapse.

sets.title: The Gardeners' Patience
sets.hook: The world is being deliberately cultivated — life here is too convenient, too AIMED — by gardeners who are present and acting but never seen. The artifacts are their shaping-tools, seeded into the soil to steer evolution; the resource is the engineered biosphere itself. The mystery: WHAT are they cultivating us FOR? Is the colony a welcome guest, a pest to be culled, or the next thing being grown?
sets.artifact_flavor: Gardeners' shaping-tools — terraforming seeds, gene-looms, soil-shrines — that let you steer or exploit the living world while possibly tripping the gardeners' attention; each reveals a little of their method and intent. The generative variable is the gardeners' INTENT per world (benevolent stewards / indifferent experimenters / breeders shaping us for a purpose / quarantiners testing whether we're safe to release), which changes whether using a tool is gratitude, theft, or playing into their plan.
sets.distinct_from_siblings: Aliens are HIDDEN and active (neither dead nor openly present — sensed, not seen), and the spine is stewardship-vs-exploitation with the player possibly BEING the experiment — a moral/ecological frame absent from the others. The subtle psychic register is its own flavor: sensing the world's 'aimed-ness' and the gardeners' watching attention (NOT time-war's precognition, NOT gen-ship's ancestral memory). Resource is core — the biosphere IS the prize — but the question is whether exploiting it is the smart move or the trap, which is the opposite of #0's exploit-and-perish certainty.
